errors: No mathematical error can be shown.
The flap table (A) has 28 labels from 1..29 with 18 absent. This is either an omission or 18 genuinely belongs to no class. Row 9 is empty.

In (B) two entries (the 5 and the 7) are overwritten. This is consistent with a corrected count, e.g. a first attempt counting complete-graph edges (6, 10) instead of triangulation edges (5, 7). That reading is conjecture.

results.what: Counts for triangulated n-gon: n vertices, 2n-3 edges, n-2 triangles (table rows 3 3 1, 4 5 2, 5 7 3)
Expressions l+1-p (bounded regions), l+3-2p (excess over triangulated polygon = interior points), l-1 in terms of points p and lines l
results.modern_name: Cyclomatic number / Euler characteristic bookkeeping for planar graphs

results.what: Classification of 28 labelled objects (1..29 without 18) into classes k=2..8 with sizes 1,6,10,6,2,2,1
results.modern_name: Valence/side-count census of a planar figure (interpretation uncertain)

deep.surprise_reason: These are scratch notes on an envelope flap: an elementary Euler-type count for triangulated polygons, and a census table whose meaning is unclear. It is presumably tied to the Gaussian-integer and lattice diagrams on adjacent leaves. Gauss's interest in planar figures and crossings (Geometria situs) is known. Nothing here goes beyond Euler-level bookkeeping.

checkable.asserts: The labels in the flap table are exactly 1..29 with 18 missing, each used once.
The weighted sum of class index times class size is 124.
Table (B) matches vertices, edges and triangles of a triangulated n-gon.
With l = 3p-3-b edges in a triangulation with b boundary vertices, l+3-2p equals the number of interior vertices p-b.
For a triangulated polygon (l=2p-3), l+3-2p=0 and l+1-p=p-2 triangles.

transcription_corrections: In the p/l table the overwritten middle entries read as corrected 5 (row 4) and 7 (row 5). The bracketed deletion marks stand for overwritten digits, not separate entries.
The header 'p l' appears to stand above the columns of the small table (points, lines). Its exact column alignment is uncertain.
The pencil numbers '14.28 54.35 / 45.12 29.26' are in a later (archival) hand, not Gauss's.
